Domain classified.evidence_source: The CAQ is an empirically sound measure of lifetime creative accomplishment in the fields of art and science. Participants check off actual achievements in 10 separate domains of creative accomplishment. Weighted scores for each domain are summed to provide a total creative achievement score (Carson et al., 2003).

section_summary.extract_value: This section details the creativity testing methods used, which included three phases: the Creativity Achievement Questionnaire (CAQ), divergent thinking tasks, and the Creative Personality Scale (CPS). The CAQ measures lifetime creative accomplishment in art and science domains, yielding a total creative achievement score. Divergent thinking tasks assessed fluency, originality, and flexibility, while the CPS involved self-description using adjectives.
section_summary.evidence_source: Creativity testing consisted of three phases: the CAQ, the divergent thinking tasks, and the CPS. CAQ. The CAQ is an empirically sound measure of lifetime creative accomplishment in the fields of art and science. Divergent thinking tasks. Four validated divergent thinking tasks were adapted from Torrance (1968). CPS. The CPS (Gough, 1979) consists of a set of 30 items from the Adjective Check List (Gough & Heilbrun, 1965).
